refinements: Dedicated hand contact and recovery palm cameras with model observation cues
Contact bounds fit actual visible palm, heel, wrist bridge, finger, thumb and nail surfaces
A fixed release-to-peak envelope prevents phase comparison from moving the camera
Camera refits after depth, lean, visible child-hand choice or viewer size changes
Recovery palm bounds include the entire enabled orientation arrow while excluding the elbow arc
Inspection clears when its target is hidden or absent in the next activity or pose
Release and peak shortcuts preserve experiment settings and recorded inquiry
Wrapped controls, keyboard reveal below the phone viewer, and system forced-color styling
coverage: Every named hand surface projects inside the close-up at adult, child and infant scale
Close-up prominence compared with the existing Hands + arms camera
Child one-to-two hand refit and changed depth/lean settings
Released versus deepest contact camera stability and retained learner state
Recovery palms and guides in flat and rolled poses at each age
320px keyboard controls, expanded text spacing, forced colors and app contrast
One app-created drawn WebGL context and cleanup on rebuild and unmount
Existing chest, limb, face, depth measurement, CPR and AED interactions
browserFixtureCorrections: The retained-focus resize test uses an 800px viewport and checks actual canvas aspect below 1 before requiring a changed camera position.
The phone recovery review brings the canvas onscreen before inspecting its rendered contrast theme, respecting the shared viewer offscreen pause.

The cadence fixture supplies exact 110bpm timestamps only during each synchronous real compression click and restores performance.now in finally. Asynchronous waits, breath timers and WebGL remain native.

reviewNotes: Reviewed each of the twelve final captures with view_image after the full browser run.
Contact views show the wrist heel, raised fingers and fitted nails with surrounding chest context.
Child peak views retain the chosen anatomy and measurement overlays as the phase changes.
Rolled recovery palms remain complete and their folds follow the hand surface.
Desktop and phone control captures show the observation cue, zoom button and release/peak actions in context.
The phone view retains wrapped controls and keyboard focus visibility with expanded text spacing.
The app contrast view preserves a clear hand silhouette and visible palm folds.
